requirements.original: The elements of the TTCN-3 syntax (reserved words, identifiers, terminal symbols and literal values) shall be separated by whitespace or by special terminal symbols listed in table A.2 according to the TTCN-3 syntax.
requirements.canonical: Elements of the TTCN-3 syntax (reserved words, identifiers, terminal symbols and literal values) SHALL be separated by whitespace or by special terminal symbols listed in table A.2, according to the TTCN-3 syntax.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.1 -- The elements of the TTCN-3 syntax (reserved words, identifiers, terminal symbols and literal values) shall be separated by whitespace or by special terminal symbols listed in table A.2 according to the TTCN-3 syntax.

requirements.original: In representing whitespace, any one or more of the following characters of the C0 set of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] and of annex A of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] may be used in any combination: HT - HORIZONTAL TABULATION (9); LF - LINE FEED (10); VT -VERTICAL TABULATION (11); FF - FORM FEED (12); CR - CARRIAGE RETURN (13); SP - SPACE (32)
requirements.canonical: Whitespace MAY consist of one or more of the ITU-T T.50 C0 characters HT (9), LF (10), VT (11), FF (12), CR (13) and SP (32) in any combination.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.1 -- In representing whitespace, any one or more of the following characters of the C0 set of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] and of annex A of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] may be used in any combination: HT - HORIZONTAL TABULATION (9); LF - LINE FEED (10); VT -VERTICAL TABULATION (11); FF - FORM FEED (12); CR - CARRIAGE RETURN (13); SP - SPACE (32)

requirements.original: The characters of the C0 set of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] and of annex A of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] below are denoting newline (end of line). LF - LINE FEED (10); VT - VERTICAL TABULATION (11); FF - FORM FEED (12); CR - CARRIAGE RETURN (13)
requirements.canonical: Each of the ITU-T T.50 C0 characters LF (10), VT (11), FF (12) and CR (13) IS a newline (end of line).
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.1 -- The characters of the C0 set of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] and of annex A of Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] below are denoting newline (end of line). LF - LINE FEED (10); VT - VERTICAL TABULATION (11); FF - FORM FEED (12); CR - CARRIAGE RETURN (13)

requirements.original: A single CR(13) character directly followed by an LF(10) character denote a single end of line (i.e. the sequence CRLFCRLFVT denotes 3 lines):
requirements.canonical: A CR (13) character directly followed by an LF (10) character IS a single end of line (e.g. the sequence CR LF CR LF VT denotes 3 lines).
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.1 -- A single CR(13) character directly followed by an LF(10) character denote a single end of line (i.e. the sequence CRLFCRLFVT denotes 3 lines):

requirements.original: Any character or character sequence that is a valid newline is also a valid whitespace.
requirements.canonical: A character or character sequence that is a valid newline IS also valid whitespace.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.1 -- Any character or character sequence that is a valid newline is also a valid whitespace.

requirements.original: @abstract @control; @decoded @default @deterministic @fuzzy; @index @lazy @local; @nocase @nodefault
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 terminals which are modifiers (table A.4) ARE: `@abstract`, `@control`, `@decoded`, `@default`, `@deterministic`, `@fuzzy`, `@index`, `@lazy`, `@local`, `@nocase` and `@nodefault`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.1 -- @abstract @control; @decoded @default @deterministic @fuzzy; @index @lazy @local; @nocase @nodefault

requirements.original: apply assert at configuration conjunct cont delta disjunct duration finished; history implies inv mode notinv now object onentry onexit; par prev realtime seq setstate static stepsize stream; timestamp until values wait
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 terminals which are reserved words in extension packages (table A.5) ARE: `apply`, `assert`, `at`, `configuration`, `conjunct`, `cont`, `delta`, `disjunct`, `duration`, `finished`, `history`, `implies`, `inv`, `mode`, `notinv`, `now`, `object`, `onentry`, `onexit`, `par`, `prev`, `realtime`, `seq`, `setstate`, `static`, `stepsize`, `stream`, `timestamp`, `until`, `values`, `wait`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.5.1 -- apply assert at configuration conjunct cont delta disjunct duration finished; history implies inv mode notinv now object onentry onexit; par prev realtime seq setstate static stepsize stream; timestamp until values wait

requirements.original: at most one UnionFieldDef of UnionDefBody or NestedUnionDef shall contain a DefaultModifier
requirements.canonical: At most one UnionFieldDef of a UnionDefBody or NestedUnionDef SHALL contain a DefaultModifier (`@default`).
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.1 -- at most one UnionFieldDef of UnionDefBody or NestedUnionDef shall contain a DefaultModifier

requirements.original: SingleExpression shall evaluate to a statically bound integer value
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression of an IntegerValueOrRange in an Enumeration SHALL evaluate to a statically bound integer value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.1 -- SingleExpression shall evaluate to a statically bound integer value

requirements.original: AllowedValues shall be of the same type as the field being subtyped
requirements.canonical: The AllowedValuesSpec of a SubTypeSpec SHALL be of the same type as the type or field being subtyped.

ambiguity.issue: 'AllowedValues' is not a production name (the production is AllowedValuesSpec); 'field being subtyped' also covers the parent type of a SubTypeDef.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.1 -- AllowedValues shall be of the same type as the field being subtyped

requirements.original: RangeDef production shall only be used with integer, charstring, universal charstring or float based types
requirements.canonical: The RangeDef production in a TemplateOrRange SHALL only be used with integer, charstring, universal charstring or float based types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.1 -- RangeDef production shall only be used with integer, charstring, universal charstring or float based types

requirements.original: When subtyping charstring or universal charstring range and values shall not be mixed in the same SubTypeSpec
requirements.canonical: When a charstring or universal charstring type is subtyped, a range and values SHALL NOT be mixed in the same SubTypeSpec.
requirements.condition: the subtyped type is charstring or universal charstring
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.1 -- When subtyping charstring or universal charstring range and values shall not be mixed in the same SubTypeSpec

requirements.original: StringLength shall only be used with String types or to limit set of and record of.
requirements.canonical: The StringLength production SHALL only be used with string types or to limit the length of record of and set of types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.1 -- StringLength shall only be used with String types or to limit set of and record of.

requirements.original: SingleExpression and Bound shall evaluate to non-negative integer values (in case of Bound including infinity)
requirements.canonical: Each SingleExpression bound of a StringLength SHALL evaluate to a non-negative integer value, and the upper bound MAY additionally be `infinity`.

ambiguity.issue: StringLength has no Bound production; 'Bound' denotes the optional upper bound (SingleExpression or InfinityKeyword).

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.1 -- SingleExpression and Bound shall evaluate to non-negative integer values (in case of Bound including infinity)

requirements.original: FormalValuePar shall resolve to an in parameter
requirements.canonical: A FormalValuePar in a TemplateOrValueFormalPar (template formal parameter list) SHALL resolve to an `in` parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- FormalValuePar shall resolve to an in parameter

requirements.original: Within BaseTemplateBody the ArrayValueOrAttrib can be used for array, record, record of and set of types.
requirements.canonical: Within a BaseTemplateBody, the ArrayValueOrAttrib alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be used' may be a plain permission or an exhaustive restriction; the parallel rule for CompoundExpression additionally lists set types. Chose the restrictive reading because it is stated as static semantics.
readings: The ArrayValueOrAttrib alternative of BaseTemplateBody SHALL only be used for array, record, record of and set of types.
The ArrayValueOrAttrib alternative of BaseTemplateBody MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types, and other types (e.g. set types) are not excluded by this rule.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- Within BaseTemplateBody the ArrayValueOrAttrib can be used for array, record, record of and set of types.

requirements.original: ExtendedIdentifier shall refer to an enumerated value with associated value
requirements.canonical: The ExtendedIdentifier of a SingleTemplateExpression that is followed by an EnumTemplateExtension SHALL refer to an enumerated value with an associated value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- ExtendedIdentifier shall refer to an enumerated value with associated value

requirements.original: each TemplateBody shall be an integer template
requirements.canonical: Each BaseTemplateBody in an EnumTemplateExtension SHALL be an integer template.

ambiguity.issue: The rule says TemplateBody while the EnumTemplateExtension production uses BaseTemplateBody.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- each TemplateBody shall be an integer template

requirements.original: the limits of each Range an integer value
requirements.canonical: The limits of each Range in an EnumTemplateExtension SHALL be integer values.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- the limits of each Range an integer value

requirements.original: PredefinedType and TypeReference shall be used for anytype value notation only.
requirements.canonical: The PredefinedType and TypeReference alternatives of a StructFieldRef SHALL be used only for anytype value notation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- PredefinedType and TypeReference shall be used for anytype value notation only.

requirements.original: PredefinedType shall not be AnyTypeKeyword.
requirements.canonical: The PredefinedType alternative of a StructFieldRef SHALL NOT be the `anytype` keyword.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- PredefinedType shall not be AnyTypeKeyword.

requirements.original: Identifier in ParRef shall be a formal parameter identifier from the associated signature definition
requirements.canonical: The Identifier in a ParRef SHALL be a formal parameter identifier from the associated signature definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- Identifier in ParRef shall be a formal parameter identifier from the associated signature definition

requirements.original: IndexRef shall be optionally used for array types and TTCN-3 record of, set of and map types.
requirements.canonical: An IndexRef MAY be used for array types and for record of, set of and map types.

ambiguity.issue: 'shall be optionally used' mixes obligation and option; it is unclear whether this restricts IndexRef to these types or merely permits it.
readings: An IndexRef MAY be used for array, record of, set of and map types.
An IndexRef SHALL only be used for array, record of, set of and map types (and, per the next sentence, string types).

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- IndexRef shall be optionally used for array types and TTCN-3 record of, set of and map types.

requirements.original: The same notation can be used for a string element reference inside an TTCN-3 charstring, universal charstring, bitstring, octetstring and hexstring type
requirements.canonical: The IndexRef notation MAY be used for a string element reference inside a charstring, universal charstring, bitstring, octetstring or hexstring value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- The same notation can be used for a string element reference inside an TTCN-3 charstring, universal charstring, bitstring, octetstring and hexstring type

requirements.original: SingleExpression will resolve to a value of integer type
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression of an IndexRef SHALL resolve to a value of integer type.

ambiguity.issue: 'will resolve' is descriptive; and the preceding rule allows IndexRef for map types, whose keys need not be integers. Chose the reading that integer indices are required except for map keys.
readings: The SingleExpression of an IndexRef SHALL resolve to an integer value for arrays, record of, set of and string types, and to a value of the key type for map types.
The SingleExpression of an IndexRef SHALL always resolve to an integer value, including for map types.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- SingleExpression will resolve to a value of integer type

requirements.original: WildcardLengthMatch shall be used when MatchingSymbol is used in fractions of a concatenated string or list (see clause 15.11)
requirements.canonical: A WildcardLengthMatch SHALL be used only when the MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.

ambiguity.issue: 'shall be used when' can mean that the length attribute is mandatory in concatenations or that it is only permitted there (the second half forbids it elsewhere).
readings: A WildcardLengthMatch SHALL be attached to AnyValue/AnyOrOmit whenever they are used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.
A WildcardLengthMatch MAY be used only when the MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- WildcardLengthMatch shall be used when MatchingSymbol is used in fractions of a concatenated string or list (see clause 15.11)

requirements.original: and shall not be used in other cases.
requirements.canonical: A WildcardLengthMatch SHALL NOT be used when the MatchingSymbol is not used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- and shall not be used in other cases.

requirements.original: In this case, the Complement, ListOfTemplates, Range, BitStringMatch, HexStringMatch, OctetStringMatch, CharStringMatch, SubsetMatch and SupersetMatch productions shall not be used.
requirements.canonical: When a MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list, the Complement, ListOfTemplates, Range, BitStringMatch, HexStringMatch, OctetStringMatch, CharStringMatch, SubsetMatch and SupersetMatch alternatives SHALL NOT be used.
requirements.condition: the MatchingSymbol is used in a fraction of a concatenated string or list

ambiguity.issue: 'In this case' may refer to the concatenation context or to the case where a WildcardLengthMatch is present; DecodedContentMatch is not listed.
readings: In a fraction of a concatenated string or list, the MatchingSymbol SHALL NOT be a Complement, ListOfTemplates, Range, BitStringMatch, HexStringMatch, OctetStringMatch, CharStringMatch, SubsetMatch or SupersetMatch.
When a WildcardLengthMatch is present, the MatchingSymbol SHALL be AnyValue or AnyOrOmit (the listed alternatives SHALL NOT be used).

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- In this case, the Complement, ListOfTemplates, Range, BitStringMatch, HexStringMatch, OctetStringMatch, CharStringMatch, SubsetMatch and SupersetMatch productions shall not be used.

requirements.original: Characters "?", "*", "\", "[", "]", "{", "}", """, "|", "(", ")", "#", "+", "d", "^", "N" have special semantics – they are metacharacters for the definition of pattern elements – only if they follow the BNF as defined above, if not they are interpreted like normal characters
requirements.canonical: The characters "?", "*", "\", "[", "]", "{", "}", """, "|", "(", ")", "#", "+", "d", "^" and "N" ARE metacharacters for the definition of pattern elements only if they follow the pattern BNF; otherwise they ARE interpreted as normal characters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- Characters "?", "*", "\", "[", "]", "{", "}", """, "|", "(", ")", "#", "+", "d", "^", "N" have special semantics – they are metacharacters for the definition of pattern elements – only if they follow the BNF as defined above, if not they are interpreted like normal characters

requirements.original: Characters "[", "-", "^", "]", "\", "q", ","have special semantics – they are metacharacters for the definition of pattern class characters – only if they follow the BNF as defined above, if not they are interpreted like normal characters
requirements.canonical: The characters "[", "-", "^", "]", "\", "q" and "," ARE metacharacters for the definition of pattern class characters only if they follow the pattern BNF; otherwise they ARE interpreted as normal characters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- Characters "[", "-", "^", "]", "\", "q", ","have special semantics – they are metacharacters for the definition of pattern class characters – only if they follow the BNF as defined above, if not they are interpreted like normal characters

requirements.original: SingleExpression shall evaluate to type integer
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression of a WildcardLengthMatch SHALL evaluate to type integer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- SingleExpression shall evaluate to type integer

requirements.original: Bounds shall evaluate to types integer, charstring, universal charstring or float.
requirements.canonical: A Bound SHALL evaluate to type integer, charstring, universal charstring or float.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- Bounds shall evaluate to types integer, charstring, universal charstring or float.

requirements.original: In case they evaluate to types charstring or universal charstring, the string length shall be
requirements.canonical: If a Bound evaluates to type charstring or universal charstring, its string length SHALL be 1.
requirements.condition: the Bound evaluates to charstring or universal charstring

ambiguity.issue: The source text is truncated after 'the string length shall be'; the required length is missing. Chose length 1 (single character), consistent with clause 6.1.2.2.
readings: If a Bound evaluates to charstring or universal charstring, its string length SHALL be 1.
If a Bound evaluates to charstring or universal charstring, its string length SHALL be some other (unstated) value or SHALL be infinity.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- In case they evaluate to types charstring or universal charstring, the string length shall be

requirements.original: infinity as lower bound and –infinity as upper bound are allowed for float types only.
requirements.canonical: `infinity` as a lower Bound and `-infinity` as an upper Bound SHALL be used only for float types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- infinity as lower bound and –infinity as upper bound are allowed for float types only.

requirements.original: if a value parameter is used, an in-line template shall evaluate to a value
requirements.canonical: If an ActualParAssignment assigns to a formal value parameter, the in-line template (TemplateInstance) SHALL evaluate to a value.
requirements.condition: the formal parameter is a value parameter

ambiguity.issue: 'value parameter' means formal value parameter; 'in-line template' denotes the TemplateInstance of the ActualParAssignment.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- if a value parameter is used, an in-line template shall evaluate to a value

requirements.original: When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type the TemplateInstance production shall resolve to one or more SingleExpressions
requirements.canonical: When the corresponding formal parameter is not a template formal parameter, the TemplateInstance of an ActualPar SHALL resolve to one or more SingleExpressions.
requirements.condition: the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type

ambiguity.issue: 'of template type' is used for a template formal parameter (there is no template type).

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.3 -- When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type the TemplateInstance production shall resolve to one or more SingleExpressions

requirements.original: the part is only optional if the FunctionRef uses the ControlKeyword and the referenced control function has no formal parameters
requirements.canonical: The parenthesized ActualParList part of a FunctionInstance SHALL be present unless the FunctionRef uses the ControlKeyword and the referenced module control function has no formal parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.4 -- the part is only optional if the FunctionRef uses the ControlKeyword and the referenced control function has no formal parameters

requirements.original: The Identifier shall be one of the pre-defined TTCN-3 function identifiers from Annex C of ETSI ES 201 873-1.
requirements.canonical: The Identifier of a PreDefFunctionIdentifier SHALL be one of the predefined TTCN-3 function identifiers from Annex C.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.4 -- The Identifier shall be one of the pre-defined TTCN-3 function identifiers from Annex C of ETSI ES 201 873-1.

requirements.original: CaseInsenModifier shall be present only if Identifier is "regexp".
requirements.canonical: A CaseInsenModifier in a PreDefFunctionIdentifier SHALL be present only if the Identifier is "regexp".
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.1.4 -- CaseInsenModifier shall be present only if Identifier is "regexp".

requirements.original: If PortRedirectSymbol is present, at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec shall be present
requirements.canonical: If the PortRedirectSymbol is present in a DoneStatement (`done` operation), at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec SHALL be present.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.4.1 -- If PortRedirectSymbol is present, at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec shall be present

requirements.original: If PortRedirectSymbol is present, at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec shall be present
requirements.canonical: If the PortRedirectSymbol is present in a KilledStatement (`killed` operation), at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec SHALL be present.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.4.1 -- If PortRedirectSymbol is present, at least one of ValueStoreSpec and IndexSpec shall be present
